His daughter Edie was at one time married to Geraldo Rivera. In his short story ―All the King‘s Horses‖ an army colonel must play a deadly game of human chess against the evil Chinese Pi Ying. Echoes" of the addressee's foot have not yet faded, nor has the "challenge-cup" been lost. This poem laments that laurel "withers quicker than the rose" and "silence sounds no worse than cheers/After earth has stopped the ears." The title character is twice carried "shoulder-high," finally being set down with a garland still on his head. Name this A.E. Housman poem commemorating the tragic end of a figure who once "won [his] town the race."

One of the two protagonists dies of typhus and leaves his parents in a ceaseless state of grief, while the object of his affection, Anna Odintsov, ends up marrying a lawyer. The other protagonist watches his father Nikolai marry Fenitchka, while he himself marries Katya and embraces life, shedding the influence of his college friend's nihilism. Such are the fates of Bazarov and Arkady Kirsanov in what novel by Ivan Turgenev?

He compares his juxtaposition of images to Paul Cezanne's foreshortening of perspective, and he wrote of staying away from drugs in The Change. After being expelled from Columbia for making obscene drawings in the dust in his dorm room, he wrote a poem about the death of his mother Naomi, and another about people "looking for an angry fix" and "starving hysterical naked." name this poet who wrote "I saw best minds of my generation destroyed by madness," author of "Kaddish" and "Howl."

He discussed the communal power of myth in the plays The New Colony and The Mountain Giants. His mature works began with the story of a man who falls off a horse and imagines that he is Henry IV, and his other meditations on the fluid nature of identity include the plays Tonight We Improvise and Right You Are, If You Think You Are. Identify this author who wrote of a family that bursts into a play rehearsal demanding to be written about in Six Characters in Search of an Author.

His works include a complaint to his purse and the triple roundel "Merciless Beauty." One of his pieces is dedicated to his son Lewis and discusses the astrolabe, while another opens with the narrator meeting Dido and Aeneas in a Temple of Glass. The pragmatism of the duck and the courtly love of the eagle are contrasted in The Parliament of Fowls, while another work starts at the Tabard Inn. Who recounted the stories of such pilgrims as the Miller and the Wife of Bath in his Canterbury Tales?

This author of the plays Van Zorn and The Porcupine received, from Theodore Roosevelt, a position at the New York Custom House in recognition of his "Captain Craig." Some of his best works are found in his collections Children of the Night and The Town Down the River. His works about the residents of Tilbury Town describe a "child of scorn" as well as a man who "glittered when he walked." name this poet of "Miniver Cheevy" and "Richard Corey."

Two characters disguise themselves as Litio and Cambio, and Vicento is dismayed to find the servant Tranio attempting another impersonation. Its first two scenes depict a practical joke in which a beggar is convinced that he is a rich nobleman, and the remainder of the play is an amusement at the beggar's putative court. Gremio and Hortensio are in a futile rivalry in, what play, in which Baptista refuses to allow Bianca to be wed until Katherina finds a husband, who turns out to be Petruchio?

He juxtaposed the characters of the Geometer and a Berber chieftain in his final book, The Wisdom of the Sands. Another of his novels centers on the decision to open up a line from Buenos Aires to Europe and Didier Daurat's choices. His first novel focused on Jacques Bernis, an air-mail delivery pilot, while another of his works revolves around someone who misses his rose, lives on B612, and has crash-landed on earth from his asteroid. Identify this author of Nightflight and The Little Prince.

It begins with a main character throwing away a copy of the dictionary while leaving Miss Pinkerton's academy. Sir Pitt lusts after that character, and Pitt's son Rawdon is a brawling captain who competes for the inheritance of Miss Crawley. Many characters go to the mainland when the Napoleonic Wars break out, and in the town of Pumpernickel, Dobbin is attacked by Amelia Sedley. Name this novel in which Jos Sedley wants to leave Becky Sharp, written by William Thackeray.

The title character is compared to a "two-legged skyrocket" and a "welter- weight cinnamon bear." This story is set in the flat town of Summit, where a character who is promised candy hits one man with a brick and decides to scalp Bill and burn Sam at the stake. Ultimately, Ebenezer Dorsest demands $250 to take back his son Johnny. Name this short story by O. Henry about the kidnapping of a boy who enjoys pretending to an Indian.

The eating of locusts in this novel symbolizes an ignorance of the danger brought by Mr. Smith's group, while the python illustrates cultural differences. The plot turns on Enoch's unmasking of an earth deity, and we hear Ezinma's father wish that she were a boy. The murder of Ikemefuna turns Nwoye away from the son of Unoka, who attempts to maintain the traditions of the Igbo people. Name this book continued in the sequel No Longer at Ease, a novel centering on Okonkwo and written by Chinua Achebe.

Stories such as "The Enchanted Spot" and "Terrible Vengeance" can be found in his Evenings on a Farm near Dikanka, which generally portrays a mythically happy world of Cossacks in this author's native Ukraine. One of his novels follows a plot by Chichikov to purchase titles to serfs, and he also wrote a short story about Platon Kuzmich Kovalyov waking up with part of his face missing. Name this author of "Nevsky Prospect" and "The Nose" who created the novel Dead Souls.

Its title comes from a book written by F. Alexander, and its first part ends with P.R. Deltoid spitting in the protagonist's face. Later, the main character is assaulted by Billyboy and Dim and left for dead after being subjected to Dr. Brodsky's Ludovico technique, which combines violent images with a drug injection. It begins with a gang of hoods sitting at the Korova milkbar, talking nadsat, and frequently discusses Beethoven's Ninth. Name this novel about the vicious Alex by Anthony Burgess.

She told Elizabeth Spencer, "I'll loiter while you solicit" in response to a sign prohibiting both actions. She later wrote a story in which a resident of China Grove leaves home to avoid her sister Stella-Rondo, as well as a novel about Dabney Fairchild's marriage and Laura McRaven's reaction. In another of her novels, a death in Mount Salus allows Laura McKelva Hand to return home. Name this author of A Curtain of Green, Delta Wedding, "Why I Live at the P.O.", and The Optimist's Daughter.

It was authorized by Robert McFarlane and was conducted in violation of the Boland Amendment. Admiral John Poindexter was convicted of obstruction of justice and Fawn Hall became the most famous secretary in the United States when she admitted to shredding documents for her boss during the hearings over this. Identify this Reagan administration scandal that made Oliver North a household name and sold arms to a Middle Eastern country in order to fund a group in Nicaragua.

His bias against foreigners is seen in his View of the Present State of Ireland and his study of neoplatonism is reflected in the "Hymn in Honor of Love." His elegy on Douglas Howard is Daphnaida, and he later wrote sonnets about his love for Elizabeth Boyle, Amoretti, and a song about his wedding to Elizabeth, Epithalamion. He used his namesake stanza for another work, featuring Artegall and the Redcrosse Knight. Identify this author who honored Elizabeth I in his 1590 The Faerie Queene.

In this work, Johnny Cashman is an old man who claims to be twenty-seven. Father Arnall's fiery sermons nearly cause the protagonist to become a Jesuit, and the boys at Clongowes Wood College wear red and white roses during academic competitions. The main figure grows suspicious of Father Moran's feelings for Emma Clery and watches his father and his aunt, Mrs. Dante Riordan, argue about Parnell. Name this novel about the aesthetic awakening of Stephen Dedalus, by James Joyce.
A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

It begins with the title character's jealous brother-in-law To-no-Chujo reading some letters. The son of Kiritsubo learns of a certain house before he goes there thanks to Myobu and Koremitsu, and later has to fend of the jealousy of Lady Rokujo after he makes love to Utsusemi and Yugao. The love affairs of the emperor's son are chronicled by Murasaki Shikibu in what book, sometimes considered the world's first novel?

A title character of this novel grew up in the coal town of Tevershall and is married to the mentally unstable Bertha Coutts. He criticizes the art of Duncan Forbes and alienates Hilda after Ivy Bolton's arrival at Wragby to care for Sir Clifford. That event allows Clifford's wife more freedom, and after a brief liaison with Michaelis she takes up with the title character, Clifford's gamekeeper. Name this novel about Connie's affair with Oliver Mellors, a work of D.H. Lawrence.

The main characters of this work are brought together by an underling who got the job through his connected uncle. One character admits drowning her child, while another was gassed in her sleep. A journalist from Rio was shot by a Mexican firing squad and spends the entirety of the play banally attempting to convince Estelle and Inez of his virtue. Name this play in which these characters become "roommates" forever, showing that "hell is other people," a work by Jean-Paul Sartre.

He worked as a ghostwriter for Jack London while laboring on his own novels such as Free Air, Our Mr. Wrenn, The Job, and The Innocents. He collaborated on such works as The Jayhawkers and the story of the rise to power of Berzelius Windrip, It Can't Happen Here. He also wrote about a man who seduces Lulu Bains and marries Cleo Benham before having Frank Shallard beaten in order to become the top preacher in Zenith. Name this author of Dodsworth and Elmer Gantry.

In this book, Elizabeth is warned that Mrs. Clay hopes to marry Sir Walter, and Louisa falls on a step and is taken to the Hardwicks, where she becomes engaged to Captain Benwick. Lady Russell advises the main character not to marry and Mrs. Smith recounts William's selfish character at Lyme Regis. That follows the protagonist's move to Bath, when Kellynch Hall is let to Admiral Croft. The relationship of Frederick Wentworth and Anne Elliot develops in what Jane Austen novel?

He wrote his Hibbert lectures during a stay at a Quaker settlement in Birmingham. His novels include Nexus and The Home and the World, which discusses Nikhil's experiences with sectarian violence. He is better known for such poetry as Wild Geese, The Golden Boat, the officially adopted work "Jana Gana Mana," and a work translated as Song Offerings. Identify this Bengali-language author of the collection Gitanjali and the Indian national anthem.

He thanked Lord Clare for a gift of game in his The Haunch of Venison and wrote a poem about a man climbing the Alps, The Traveller. He created characters like Croaker and Mr. Honeywood in the comedy The Good-Natur'd Man, while another work, featuring Tony Lumpkin and the Hardcastles, and one of his novels turns on the struggle between Squire Thornhill and the family of Dr. Primrose. Identify this author of "The Deserted Village," The Vicar of Wakefield, and She Stoops to Conquer.

He sporadically issued parts of his only novel under such titles as The Fifth Book and Ringing Island. He wrote about an abbey whose constitution states "do what you will," the Thelemite order, as well as such characters as Badebec and Friar John, after Francis I licensed this former monk and doctor to print his story about the descendants of Grandgousier. Name this French humanist who used the anagram Alcofribas Nasier to publish the tale of two humanoid giants, Gargantua and Pantagruel.

One of his novels discusses Miriam Schaefer's designs to have Brother Antonio killed by a man calling himself Donatello. In a short story by this author, Robin sees a relative tarred and feathered. He burned his story collection Seven Tales of My Native Land and paid to have his first novel Fanshawe published. Name this author of "The Great Carbuncle," "Dr. Heidegger's Experiment," and "Rappacini's Daughter," who wrote about Governor Bellingham and Arthur Dimmesdale in The Scarlet Letter.

He wrote of a journey to Halba and Gebel in one novel, while another book features a woman of the night named Nur and a bar owner named Tarzan. That work, The Thief and the Dogs, was preceded by the naturalistic Children of Gebalawi. He is likely better known for discussing various generations of the al-Jawad family in Sugar Street, Palace of Desire, and Palace Walk. Name this author of the Cairo Trilogy.

He disguises himself as a fortune teller named Old Mother Bunches, and in that capacity he disappoints Blanche Ingram, a socialite who hopes to marry him for his money. He once had an affair with the French opera singer Celine Varens, and he pays Grace Poole to keep his wife under control on the hidden upper floor. Name this husband of the unstable Bertha Mason who ultimately marries Jane Eyre.

Written in quatrains, it is thought to be a meditation on the early death of the poet's friend Richard West. The titular place, where "full many a flower is born to blush unseen," was probably located in Stoke Poges, where the poet's family members were buried. Identify this work set "Far from the madding crowd's ignoble strife" that begins "The curfew tolls the knell of parting day," written by Thomas Gray.
Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

This novel ends after a loveless romantic encounter with Professor Irwin and a return to school. Buddy Willard cheats on the main character, who envisions her life as a fig tree that ends either in marriage or loneliness. Things go from bad to worse for the protagonist after she is sent to Dr. Gordon, who gives her electric shock therapy. The pen name Victoria Lucas was used for what novel about the mental breakdown and recovery of Esther Greenwood, by Sylvia Plath?

In this work, the author asks for a beaker of Hippocrene, and the musk rose is described as being "mid-May's eldest child." The eighth line of each stanza is written in trimeter, and this poem compares the word "forlorn" to a bell. The author states that the homesick Ruth heard the title figure's song in this poem, containing the lines "tender is the night" and "Thou wast not born for death, immortal Bird." name this poem by John Keats.
